name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year; next release 4 Dec
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, down 1.6 points (1.2%) from a revised September level and 5.9% above October 2025 (FAO, 6 Nov). That is below the 135 Alert line but meets the Watch line on the annual rise. No new export bans on a staple by several major exporters were found as of 11 Nov; the next release is due on 4 Dec.
for_you: Global food commodity prices feed into UK shop prices with a lag of several months, so grocery inflation tends to stay firm for a while after an index rise. Households on tight budgets are most exposed.
rubric_hit: FFPI 133.9 in 120–135 Watch band; y/y +5.9% > +5% Watch line

sources.title: FAO — FAO Food Price Index edges down in October amid subdued demand

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
